en.title: Superstitions and sayings
en.summary: Lucky and unlucky beliefs and common proverbs.

paragraphs: Superstitions are beliefs that certain actions bring luck or bad luck, and proverbs are short sayings that give advice. This lesson introduces both and the zero conditional used to state general truths.

Many English-speaking people avoid walking under a ladder, think that breaking a mirror brings seven years of bad luck and consider Friday the thirteenth unlucky. Good luck comes from finding a four-leaf clover or touching wood. Few people believe these things seriously, but many follow them for fun. Two friends pass a ladder on Friday the thirteenth.

lines.speaker: Abby
lines.text: I'm not walking under that ladder.

lines.speaker: Abby
lines.text: A little. It's bad luck, and today's Friday the thirteenth.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: My gran says, if you break a mirror, you get seven years of bad luck.

lines.speaker: Abby
lines.text: Mine says, if you see a magpie, you should say hello to it.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: She also says, a stitch in time saves nine.

lines.speaker: Abby
lines.text: That's a proverb, not a superstition.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Yes, it means you should repair a small problem before it becomes big.

paragraphs: **1. The zero conditional states general truths.** Use if + present simple, present simple. It describes what always happens. See Introduction to Grammar: Moods, command, subjunctive and conditional.

blocks.html:
If-clauseResult
If you break a mirror,you get bad luck.
If you find a clover,you have good luck.
If you walk under a ladder,something bad happens.
If you touch wood,you avoid bad luck.

paragraphs: **2. Proverbs are fixed.** Their words do not change, and they use short, memorable structures. Learn them as units and use them for effect. See Introduction to Grammar: Sentence structure.

blocks.html:
ProverbMeaning
A stitch in time saves nine.act early to avoid bigger problems
Every cloud has a silver lining.bad things have good sides
Don't count your chickens before they hatch.don't be too sure of success
The early bird catches the worm.the person who acts first gains

items: Black cats are lucky in Britain but unlucky in the United States.
Touch wood (or knock on wood) is said to avoid bad luck.
Friday the thirteenth is thought unlucky.
Superstitious means believing in luck and omens.

paragraphs: Some buildings have no thirteenth floor, and some aeroplanes have no row thirteen. Proverbs are used in conversation to make a point briefly, often with a smile.
